1088/1757-899X/868/1/012009 The application of radar absorbing materials to reduce interference emissions from instruments and devices of spacecraft electrical systems P A Zhukov* and V Yu Kirillov Department of Theoretical Electrical Engineering, Moscow Aviation Institute (National Research University), 4 Volokolamskoe shosse, Moscow 125993, Russia *E-mail: kaf309@mai
The study of interference emissions, the model of the spacecraft module in the case when the radio-absorbing material TPMV-1C is placed in the internal space of the module model is carried out
The expediency of using the TPMV-1C radar absorbing material to reduce the interference emissions of on-board instruments and devices of electrical systems of spacecraft is shown

Introduction To ensure electromagnetic compatibility of instruments and devices of the electrical systems of spacecraft, it is necessary to reduce the interference emissions of airborne instruments and devices [1]

An electromagnetic field with high intensity acts on-board electronic devices, worsens the quality of their functioning and creates conditions for failures and irreversible violations in their work [2-4]
One of the common ways to reduce interference emissions is the use of electromagnetic shields [5]
Electromagnetic shields have inhomogeneities and apertures and therefore cannot always provide an effective reduction in interference emissions [6-8]

To reduce the interference emissions and, accordingly, to increase the efficiency of shielding, in cases where the capabilities of the electromagnetic shield are fully used, it is possible to use radar absorbing materials (RAM) [9]

At present, radar-absorbing materials studied in solving scientific problems [10-14], but these studies not intended to use radar-absorbing materials on board spacecraft to reduce interference emissions
Radar-absorbing materials placed in the module of the spacecraft must save their electrophysical properties in the temperature range from –150 to +150ºC
